summary: DFM-Fusion (optimized) achieves multi-hop F1=18.72, slightly exceeding LLM-Fusion (18.63) and statistically significantly outperforming No-Fusion (17.10). The three-tier decision rule maps to 'Continue/Proceed': DFM-Fusion is not statistically worse than LLM-Fusion (paired t-test p=0.864, bootstrap 95% CI [-0.010, +0.012] includes 0) AND is statistically better than No-Fusion (p=0.031, CI [+0.003, +0.031] excludes 0). Gap recovery is 106.4%. The deterministic, zero-LLM-call fusion operator fully replaces the LLM-guided fusion on LoCoMo multi-hop F1 without any performance loss.
analysis: Three experimental conditions were evaluated on LoCoMo-10 (1986 QAs, 3 runs each). DFM-Fusion (optimized) achieves multi-hop F1=0.1872+/-0.0034, LLM-Fusion=0.1863+/-0.0021, No-Fusion=0.1710+/-0.0009. Paired statistical tests on 282 multi-hop questions (averaged across 3 runs) show: (1) DFM vs LLM: mean diff=+0.0010, t=0.172, p=0.864, bootstrap 95% CI=[-0.010, +0.012] — no significant difference. (2) DFM vs No-Fusion: mean diff=+0.0162, t=2.172, p=0.031, bootstrap 95% CI=[+0.003, +0.031] — statistically significant improvement. (3) LLM vs No-Fusion: mean diff=+0.0152, t=2.001, p=0.046 — confirming fusion gap exists. Per-category analysis: DFM-Fusion matches LLM-Fusion closely on multi-hop (18.72 vs 18.63), single-hop (34.18 vs 34.22), temporal (5.91 vs 6.14), and adversarial (85.79 vs 86.05). The only category with a visible gap is open-domain (10.19 vs 10.68), but this is a small absolute difference on 96 questions. Practical benefits: DFM-Fusion uses zero additional LLM calls (vs 226 for LLM-Fusion per run), is fully deterministic and auditable, and runs at comparable wall-clock time.
reason: Verdict is 'good' because: (1) Both the main experiment (DFM-Fusion) and baselines (LLM-Fusion, No-Fusion) ran successfully and produced results. (2) DFM-Fusion meets the Continue/Proceed tier of the pre-specified decision rule — it is not statistically worse than LLM-Fusion AND is statistically better than No-Fusion. (3) Gap recovery is 106.4%, meaning DFM-Fusion fully recovers (and slightly exceeds) the performance gap that LLM-based fusion provides. (4) The method achieves this with zero extra LLM calls, full determinism, and auditability. This is a positive result confirming the hypothesis that LLM-based fusion is unnecessary for LoCoMo multi-hop QA when replaced with the proposed deterministic sentence-level dedup + MMR packing approach.
